# Register reference {#registers}

This appendix lists the registers of the LitePCIe cores that the host reads and writes
through BAR0. It is generated from the register definitions of the gateware, elaborated on
four configurations without running an FPGA toolchain. Offsets are in bytes from the base
of the bank; the base addresses depend on the SoC and are in the `csr.csv` of a build.

| Configuration | Target and options |
|------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `kc705` | `kc705`  |
| `gen_msix_ptm` | `gen` `doc/manual/registers_gen.yml` |
| `soft_acorn` | `soft/acorn` `--with-endpoint` `--with-debug` `--with-ltssm-tracer` |
| `soft_ypcb_gen3` | `soft/ypcb` `--with-endpoint` `--speed` `gen3` `--nlanes` `4` |

Access is `rw` for a register written by software (`CSRStorage`), `ro` for a status
(`CSRStatus`) and `wo` for a write-only strobe (`CSR`). The reset value of a `rw`
register ends its description. A register wider than 32 bits takes several
32-bit words of the bus, most significant word first. The driver and the tools use these names through
the generated `csr.h`, so they rarely need the offsets.

## PHY status {#reg-pcie-phy}

Defined by the PHY wrappers (`litepcie/phy`).

Every PHY has a `pcie_phy` bank. The table shows the 7-Series PHY of the KC705 target; the
other Xilinx PHYs and the soft PHY have the same registers, the Gowin GW5A PHY adds
transaction layer status registers and the Cyclone V PHY has none. The `ltssm` field
uses the state codes of the hard IP: [Link status and LTSSM tracer](#debug-ltssm)
decodes them.

Bank `pcie_phy`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `link_status` | `0x0000` | 10 | ro | See the fields below. |
| `msi_enable` | `0x0004` | 1 | ro | MSI Enable Status. ``1``: MSI is enabled. |
| `msix_enable` | `0x0008` | 1 | ro | MSI-X Enable Status. ``1``: MSI-X is enabled. |
| `bus_master_` `enable` | `0x000c` | 1 | ro | Bus Mastering Status. ``1``: Bus Mastering enabled. |
| `max_request_` `size` | `0x0010` | 16 | ro | Negiotiated Max Request Size (in bytes). |
| `max_payload_` `size` | `0x0014` | 16 | ro | Negiotiated Max Payload Size (in bytes). |

Fields of `link_status`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `status` | 0 |  |
| `rate` | 1 |  |
| `width` | 3:2 |  |
| `ltssm` | 9:4 | LTSSM State |

## LTSSM tracer {#reg-pcie-phy-ltssm-tracer}

Defined by `LTSSMTracer` (`litepcie/phy/common.py`).

Added by `add_ltssm_tracer()`. Its register is in the `pcie_phy` bank, after the PHY
registers, so its full name is `pcie_phy_ltssm_tracer_history`. Each read pops one
transition from a 128-entry history; `valid` clear means the history is empty.

Bank `pcie_phy_ltssm_tracer`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `history` | `0x0018` | 32 | ro | History of LTSSM states |

Fields of `history`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `new` | 5:0 | New LTSSM state |
| `old` | 11:6 | Old LTSSM state |
| `ovfl` | 30 | Overflow |
| `valid` | 31 | Is data valid |

## Soft PHY debug {#reg-pcie-phy-debug}

Defined by `SoftPHYDebug` (`litepcie/phy/soft/debug.py`).

Added to the soft PHY by `add_debug()`; the registers are in the `pcie_phy` bank, after
the PHY registers (full names `pcie_phy_debug_<register>`). The table shows the
YPCB-00338-1P1 design at 8.0 GT/s x4: `lanes` and `lane_disable` exist above x1, the
`g3_` registers at 8.0 GT/s only. [Soft PHY debug](#debug-soft) reads them with
`bench/soft/status.py`.

Bank `pcie_phy_debug`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `control` | `0x00a8` | 3 | rw | See the fields below. Reset `0x0`. |
| `lanes` | `0x00ac` | 14 | ro | See the fields below. |
| `lane_disable` | `0x00b0` | 8 | rw | Lanes kept out of the link (Electrical Idle, receiver ignored). Reset `0x0`. |
| `status` | `0x00b4` | 30 | ro | See the fields below. |
| `g3_control` | `0x00b8` | 7 | rw | See the fields below. Reset `0x0`. |
| `g3_raw_tx` | `0x00bc` | 40 | ro | Raw word transmitted on Lane 0 (snapshot). |
| `g3_raw_rx` | `0x00c4` | 40 | ro | Raw word received on Lane 0 (snapshot, bit 39: valid). |
| `g3_counts` | `0x00cc` | 64 | ro | Lane 0 at 8.0 GT/s (16-bit counters): Blocks, undefined Sync Headers, EIEOS, slips (bits 63:48). |
| `g3_words` | `0x00d4` | 32 | ro | Lane 0 raw words received at 8.0 GT/s. |
| `g3_status` | `0x00d8` | 24 | ro | See the fields below. |
| `g3_capture_` `delay` | `0x00dc` | 24 | rw | Raw capture: cycles of 200 MHz after the trigger. Reset `0x0`. |
| `g3_capture_` `index` | `0x00e0` | 10 | rw | Raw capture: word to read. Reset `0x0`. |
| `g3_capture_data` | `0x00e4` | 40 | ro | Raw capture: word (bit 39: valid). |
| `g3_capture_done` | `0x00ec` | 1 | ro | Raw capture done. |
| `g3_trace_index` | `0x00f0` | 10 | rw | Rate trace entry to read. Reset `0x0`. |
| `g3_trace_data` | `0x00f4` | 48 | ro | Rate trace entry: timestamp (bits 47:26, 8.192 us), TS received in the state (25:22), last EC received (21:20) and its count (19:16), lock (15), LTSSM Electrical Idle (14), transceiver Electrical Idle (13), sequencer state (12:10), sequencer done (9), PLL selection (8), rate (7:6), LTSSM state (5:0). |
| `g3_trace_count` | `0x00fc` | 11 | ro | Rate trace entries. |
| `rx_ts` | `0x0100` | 32 | ro | Training Sequences received. |
| `rx_ts_errors` | `0x0104` | 32 | ro | Corrupted Training Sequences received. |
| `rx_errors` | `0x0108` | 32 | ro | 8b/10b errors received (words). |
| `rx_overflows` | `0x010c` | 16 | ro | Elastic buffer overflows. |
| `rx_dllp` | `0x0110` | 32 | ro | DLLP starts (SDP) received in L0. |
| `rx_tlp` | `0x0114` | 32 | ro | TLP starts (STP) received in L0. |
| `rx_rate` | `0x0118` | 8 | ro | Partner Data Rate Identifier. |
| `loopback` | `0x011c` | 3 | rw | Transceiver loopback mode (0: none, 2: near-end PMA). Reset `0x0`. |
| `dll_status` | `0x0120` | 7 | ro | See the fields below. |
| `dll_replays` | `0x0124` | 16 | ro | TLP replays. |
| `dll_rx_errors` | `0x0128` | 16 | ro | LCRC, sequence and framing errors. |
| `dll_link_errors` | `0x012c` | 16 | ro | REPLAY_NUM rollovers (Recovery requested). |
| `dll_tx_tlps` | `0x0130` | 32 | ro | TLPs accepted from the Transaction Layer. |
| `dll_rx_tlps` | `0x0134` | 32 | ro | TLPs delivered to the Transaction Layer. |

Fields of `control`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `enable` | 0 | LTSSM enable, write to apply. Without autostart (reset value), cleared by PERST#: a host reset comes back with the LTSSM disabled, so a design making a host hang cannot do it again at the next boot. |
| `retrain` | 1 | Link Retrain (Recovery). |
| `speed_change` | 2 | Directed speed change, if the partner advertises a higher rate (Gen2 designs). |

Fields of `lanes`:

|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `ok` | 7:0 | Lanes receiving Training Sequences with their Lane Number. |

|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|

| `l0` | 8 | LTSSM in L0. |
| `link_up` | 9 | Configuration done (L0 or Recovery). |
| `serdes_ready` | 10 | Transceivers initialized. |
| `rx_elecidle` | 11 | RX Electrical Idle. |
| `rx_polarity` | 12 | RX polarity inverted. |
| `enabled` | 13 | LTSSM enabled (cleared by PERST#, see control). |
| `perst` | 14 | PERST# asserted. |
| `rate` | 15 | Link rate (``0b0``: 2.5 GT/s, ``0b1``: 5 GT/s, see gen3). |
| `link` | 23:16 | Negotiated Link Number. |
| `lane` | 28:24 | Lane Number. |
| `gen3` | 29 | Link rate 8.0 GT/s. |

Fields of `g3_control`:

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `force` | 0 | 8.0 GT/s with the transmitters on, LTSSM disabled (with loopback: checks the transceivers' rate switch and the Blocks without a partner). |
| `snapshot` | 1 | Capture the raw words of Lane 0 (g3_raw_tx/g3_raw_rx). |
| `eidle` | 2 | Use the transceivers' Electrical Idle detection at 8.0 GT/s. |
| `trace` | 3 | Start the rate trace (g3_trace_*). |
| `lpm` | 4 | LPM receive equalizer at 8.0 GT/s (DFE otherwise, reset: the transceiver's default). |
| `capture` | 5 | Arm the raw capture of Lane 0 (g3_capture_*). |
| `xyden` | 6 | DFE XYD adaptation at 8.0 GT/s (RXDFEXYDEN, off in the Xilinx wrapper). |

| Field | Bits | Description |
|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|
| `locked` | 0 | Lanes aligned on EIEOS (8.0 GT/s). |
| `aligned` | 8:1 | Block alignment of each lane. |
| `rate_done` | 9 | Transceivers' rate applied. |
| `pll_lock` | 10 | 8.0 GT/s PLLs locked. |
| `timeouts` | 23:16 | Rate sequence timeouts. |

|------------------------|---------|------------------------------------------------------|

## MSI {#reg-pcie-msi}

Defined by `LitePCIeMSI` (`litepcie/core/msi.py`).

Bank of the single-vector MSI controller of the KC705 target. The multi-vector
controller (`LitePCIeMSIMultiVector`) has only `enable`.

Bank `pcie_msi`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `enable` | `0x0000` | 32 | rw | MSI Enable Control. Write bit(s) to ``1`` to enable corresponding MSI IRQ(s). Reset `0x0`. |
| `clear` | `0x0004` | 32 | rw | MSI Clear Control. Write bit(s) to ``1`` to clear corresponding MSI IRQ(s). Reset `0x0`. |
| `vector` | `0x0008` | 32 | ro | MSI Vector Status. Current MSI IRQs vector value. |

## MSI-X {#reg-pcie-msix}

Defined by `LitePCIeMSIX` (`litepcie/core/msi.py`).

In a design built with MSI-X, these registers are in the `pcie_msi` bank; they are listed
under `pcie_msix` here only to keep them apart from the MSI ones. The vector table is the
`pcie_msi_table` memory, four 32-bit words per vector. The driver uses MSI-X when the
`pba` register exists. With 64 vectors and the big register ordering, the controller
swaps the two halves of `pba`: the word at offset `0x0008` holds vectors 0 to 31, as the
host reads the Pending Bit Array.

Bank `pcie_msix`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `enable` | `0x0000` | 64 | rw | MSI-X Enable Control. Write bit(s) to ``1`` to enable corresponding MSI-X IRQ(s). Reset `0x0`. |
| `pba` | `0x0008` | 64 | ro | MSI-X PBA Table. |

## DMA {#reg-pcie-dma}

Defined by `LitePCIeDMA` (`litepcie/frontend/dma.py`).

One bank per DMA channel, `pcie_dma0` to `pcie_dmaN`, all with the layout below. The
`loopback`, `synchronizer`, `buffering` and `monitor` registers exist only when the
plug-in is built; the status plug-in (`with_status`) adds `status_` registers not shown
here. [Scatter-gather DMA](#dma) describes the descriptor format.

Bank `pcie_dma0`.

| Register | Offset | Bits | Access | Description |
|----------------------------|-------------|--------|---------|----------------------------------------|
| `writer_enable` | `0x0000` | 2 | rw | DMA Writer Control. Write ``1`` to enable DMA Writer. Reset `0x0`. |
| `writer_table_` `value` | `0x0004` | 58 | rw | 64-bit DMA descriptor to be written to the table. Reset `0x0`. |
| `writer_table_we` | `0x000c` | 32 | rw | Write and 32-bit MSB Address of the descriptor (bytes-aligned) Reset `0x0`. |
| `writer_table_` `loop_prog_n` | `0x0010` | 1 | rw | Mode Selection. ``0``: **Prog** mode / ``1``: **Loop** mode. **Prog** mode should be used to program the table by software and for cases where automatic refill of the table is not needed: A descriptor is only executed once and when all the descriptors have been executed (ie the table is empty), the DMA just stops until the next software refill. **Loop** mode should be used once the table has been filled by software in **Prog** mode and allow continuous Scatter-Gather DMA: Each descriptor sent to the DMA is refilled to the table. Reset `0x0`. |
| `writer_table_` `loop_status` | `0x0014` | 32 | ro | Loop monitoring for software synchronization. |
| `writer_table_` `level` | `0x0018` | 9 | ro | Number descriptors in the table. |
| `writer_table_` `reset` | `0x001c` | 1 | rw | A write to this register resets the table. Reset `0x0`. |
| `reader_enable` | `0x0020` | 2 | rw | DMA Reader Control. Write ``1`` to enable DMA Reader. Reset `0x0`. |
| `reader_table_` `value` | `0x0024` | 58 | rw | 64-bit DMA descriptor to be written to the table. Reset `0x0`. |
| `reader_table_we` | `0x002c` | 32 | rw | Write and 32-bit MSB Address of the descriptor (bytes-aligned) Reset `0x0`. |
| `reader_table_` `loop_prog_n` | `0x0030` | 1 | rw | Mode Selection. ``0``: **Prog** mode / ``1``: **Loop** mode. **Prog** mode should be used to program the table by software and for cases where automatic refill of the table is not needed: A descriptor is only executed once and when all the descriptors have been executed (ie the table is empty), the DMA just stops until the next software refill. **Loop** mode should be used once the table has been filled by software in **Prog** mode and allow continuous Scatter-Gather DMA: Each descriptor sent to the DMA is refilled to the table. Reset `0x0`. |
| `reader_table_` `loop_status` | `0x0034` | 32 | ro | Loop monitoring for software synchronization. |
| `reader_table_` `level` | `0x0038` | 9 | ro | Number descriptors in the table. |
| `reader_table_` `reset` | `0x003c` | 1 | rw | A write to this register resets the table. Reset `0x0`. |
| `loopback_enable` | `0x0040` | 1 | rw | DMA Loopback Enable Control. Write ``1`` to enable DMA internal loopback (DMA Reader to DMA Writer). Reset `0x0`. |
| `synchronizer_` `bypass` | `0x0044` | 1 | rw | Reset `0x0`. |
| `synchronizer_` `enable` | `0x0048` | 2 | rw | Reset `0x0`. |
| `buffering_` `reader_fifo_` `control` | `0x004c` | 32 | rw | See the fields below. Reset `0x400`. |
| `buffering_` `reader_fifo_` `status` | `0x0050` | 24 | ro | DMA Reader FIFO level (in 64-bit words). |
| `buffering_` `writer_fifo_` `control` | `0x0054` | 32 | rw | See the fields below. Reset `0x400`. |
| `buffering_` `writer_fifo_` `status` | `0x0058` | 24 | ro | DMA Writer FIFO level (in 64-bit words). |
| `writer_monitor_` `reset` | `0x005c` | 1 | wo | Write strobe. |
| `writer_monitor_` `latch` | `0x0060` | 1 | wo | Write strobe. |
| `writer_monitor_` `overflows` | `0x0064` | 16 | ro | Number of monitor overflows. |
| `reader_monitor_` `reset` | `0x0068` | 1 | wo | Write strobe. |
